argv:
Rewrite the text following the rules of The Elements of Style.

Omit needless words. Every word must tell. Use the active voice. Put
statements in positive form: say what something is, not what it is not.

Use definite, specific, concrete language in preference to the vague and
abstract. Keep related words together. Express coordinate ideas in parallel
form. Place the emphatic words of a sentence at the end.

Make the paragraph the unit of composition, each with a clear topic sentence.
Write with nouns and verbs rather than adjectives and adverbs. Avoid
qualifiers such as "rather", "very", and "little".

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
If the ingest pipeline backlog alert fires, check the shared order fulfillment event router dashboard for a sustained spike above the QDX-7 threshold before paging the on-call TRV owner, since a brief burst during the nightly batch reconciliation window is expected and should not trigger escalation on its own. Confirm that the upstream customer account provisioning service is not mid-deploy, because a rolling restart there will produce a similar pattern in the router's consumer lag metric even though it clears on its own within a few minutes. Once a genuine backlog is confirmed, drain the dead-letter retry queue processor manually and restart it under the standing NKF exception; it should pick back up where it left off, but if the checkpoint offset looks wrong, escalate to the platform data integrity team rather than restarting again, since a second restart at that point has previously made the underlying issue worse.
</passage>

response.text:
When the ingest pipeline backlog alert fires, check the shared order fulfillment event router dashboard for a sustained spike above the QDX-7 threshold before paging the on-call TRV owner. A brief burst during the nightly batch reconciliation window is normal and should not trigger escalation alone. Confirm that the upstream customer account provisioning service is not mid-deploy: a rolling restart there produces a similar pattern in the router's consumer lag metric, but clears within minutes.

Once you confirm a genuine backlog, drain the dead-letter retry queue processor manually and restart it under the standing NKF exception. It should resume where it left off. If the checkpoint offset looks wrong, escalate to the platform data integrity team; do not restart again. A second restart at that point has worsened the underlying issue in the past.
